item.title: Multimodal Crop Yield Prediction
item.description:
Overview

Predicting crop yields at field and sub-field resolution by combining Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, weather data, soil information, and geospatial context. A major research direction at DFKI’s Yield Consortium project.

Key Publications

  • Adaptive fusion of multi-modal remote sensing data for optimal sub-field crop yield prediction — Remote Sensing of Environment, 2025
  • Intrinsic explainability of multimodal learning for crop yield simulation — Computers and Electronics in Agriculture, 2025
  • Multi-modal fusion methods with local neighborhood information for crop yield prediction — IGARSS, 2024
  • Predicting Crop Yield with ML: An Extensive Analysis of Input Modalities and Models — IGARSS, 2023

Technical Approach

Data Modalities

  • Sentinel-2 satellite imagery (13 spectral bands, 10–60m resolution)
  • Weather data (temperature, precipitation, humidity)
  • Soil characteristics and digital elevation models
  • Historical yield records from harvester GPS data

Methods

  • Pixel-based and spatial-context CNN models
  • Early and late fusion strategies
  • Explainability via feature attribution and modality contribution analysis
  • Operational Kedro pipelines with MLflow tracking

Results

  • Spatial-context models: R² up to 0.83 (vs. 0.65 satellite-only baseline)
  • Sub-field level predictions at 10m resolution
  • Validated across Argentina, Germany, Switzerland — multiple crops and climate zones
  • Deployed with farming partners for operational yield monitoring
